title: Level 5 (World Class) - A-8
notes:
West leads the ♥J against 3NT. West's opening heart lead is won by South. South does not have time to establish the diamonds as the defense will be able to cash their hearts first. South must play on clubs, but if a trick has to be lost in that suit, dummy's lack of a quick side entry could spell trouble.

South can resolve his communication problem and virtually guarantee the contract with a jettison play. South should cash his top spades pitching diamonds from the dummy (cashing only 1 high spade also works). The top clubs are cashed next. If the ♣Q is still outstanding, South concedes a club trick as he discards his other heart honour.

The defense can no longer attack hearts without giving dummy an entry. If the defense plays either spades or diamonds, the South hand will become high and only 3 more tricks will be lost.
